policies.title: Tanzanian ordinary passports: Grenada visitor visa waiver
policies.summary: Grenada's active Embassy-linked nationality schedule lists Tanzania as not requiring a visa.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Tanzanian passport holder travelling as a short visitor.
The active Embassy schedule was updated April 2024 and should be rechecked if Grenada publishes a replacement.
Work, study, residence, transit, special documents and final admission remain outside scope.

policies.title: Tanzanian ordinary passports: Panama authorized visitor visa
policies.summary: Panama's live Embassy schedule places Tanzania in its authorized-visa cohort for advance immigration approval.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Tanzanian passport holder who does not qualify for Panama's separate third-country visa or residence waiver.
Authorized-visa approval may take up to 60 business days and must be granted before travel.
Washington-specific filing mechanics are not generalized to every consular district; final admission remains discretionary.

conflicts.explanation: The current B-1/B-2 entry and visa-issuance suspension retains valid-visa grandfathering, specified exceptions and case-by-case waivers, so it cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The partial suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes Puerto Rico. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The partial suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes Guam. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The partial suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes the Northern Mariana Islands. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The partial suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes the U.S. Virgin Islands. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
